English: Salt Lick
A simple salt-encrusted rock or shallow pit that herders use to attract and maintain their herds. Essential for livestock health and nomad sustenance.
Salt Pit
Primitive excavations in salt-rich ground, these pits allow nomads to gather greater quantities of salt, vital for both animals and trade.
Salt Shed
A sturdy timber and hide structure for storing harvested salt, protecting it from the elements and pilfering, and ensuring stable supplies for the horde.
Stone Storage
A reinforced stone storehouse, insulated to protect large salt reserves from dampness. Enables more ambitious logistics and trade.
Salt Pavilion
A grand tented pavilion for the overseers of the salt trade, serving as a hub for salt merchants and caravan leaders. Marks the start of organized salt commerce.
Market Stand
A bustling cluster of trading stalls, where salt is exchanged for goods, livestock, and favors. Increases the hordes wealth and draws merchants from far and wide.
Expanded Hall
A large semi-permanent hall of timber and stone, where salt traders and clan leaders meet to set prices and policies. Centralizes salt trade and enhances population support.
Traders Pavilion
A lavish tented complex for foreign merchants, with secure storage, meeting tents, and guards. Boosts salt trade revenue and increases movement along trade routes.
Salt Guildhall
A fortified compound for the salt merchant guild, with its own guards, bookkeepers, and trading courts. Oversees all salt commerce and clan agreements.
Tibetan Salt Guild

The supreme authority in salt trade for the entire region, with a sprawling compound, courts, watchtowers, and caravansaries. Dictates salt policy and ensures the hordes dominance in the lucrative salt routes.
